parties:
Farida Begum Minu and Others
Vs.
Abdul Jabbar Being Dead His Heirs Md. Nurul Amin and Others
full_judgment:
2. Short facts of the case are as follows:-The opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs on 24.01.93 filed Title Suit No. 278 of 1993 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, against the defendants petitioners and the opposite party Nos. 3-9, praying for declaration of title in respect of Ka schedule land and further declaration that Kha schedule Heba deed is illegal, void, inoperatives, not binding upon plaintiffs and for recovery of khan possession in respect of Ga schedule property described in the schedule of the plaint, stating in short that the suit land appertaining to C.S. khatian No. 569, Plot No. 138, measuring an area of land of 2.04 acre and C.S. Plot No. 590 measuring an area of land of 0.33 acre belonged to Wahed Ali and others. The mother of plaintiff No. 1 Chandraban Bibi purchased the land by auction. Thereafter, Chandraban Bibi transferred the land 2.04 acre from the plot No. 138 on 14.09.1949 vide Heba-Bil-Ewaj deed No. 4367 to her two sons Abdul Karim and plaintiff No. 1 Abdul Jabbar. In that deed plot No. 168 has been written erroneously instead of the plot No. 138. Chandraban Bibi had not right, title and ownership over the plot No. 168. The plaintiff No. 1 and his brother owned and possessed the suit land. S.A. khatian No. 667 has been prepared in their names. Plaintiff No. 1 and his brother Abdul Karim transferred 23 decimals land from the plot No. 138 to Intezam and others and they have been owning and possessing that land. Thereafter Government of Bangladesh acquired 89 decimal land from the plot No. 138 by L.A. Case No.159/61-62 Award was prepared in the name of Chandraban, and the plaintiff No.1 and his brother Abdul Karim withdrew the compensation money. Chandraban sold 35 decimals of land from the plot No. 590 to Mather Box and others on 01.09.49 and 85 decimals of land remained in the plot No. 138 which was owned and possessed by the plaintiff No. 1 and his brother Abdul Karim. Thereafter, Abdul Karim died in 1971 laying behind 3 sons, namely, Badsha Miah, Lal Mia and Kokhu Miah and 3 daughters, namely, Samala Khatun, Jamila Khatun and Jahanara Khatun. The defendant No. 4-9 owned 42½  decimals of land from their predecessor, the defendant No. 2,6,7 and 9 sold 21.3333 decimals of land to the plaintiff No. 1 on 23.03.79 vide registered deed No.1053. Defendant No. 4,5 and 6 were minors. Defendant No. 2 was appointed guardian in favour of the defendant No. 4,5,8 by the learned District Judge and with the permission of the Court, defendant No. 2 as a guardian sold 21½ decimals of land in favour of the plaintiff No. 1 on 18.07.1979 vide registered deed No. 3108. In this way the heirs of Abdul Karim sold their 42½  decimals of land. The plaintiff No. 1 has owned .64 decimals of land by way of purchase and gift. The plaintiffs mutated their names and paid rent to the Government and tax to the Municipality and they got Gas line, Water line and paid all rent. The plaintiff approved a plan from DIT (now RAJUK) for constructing building. The plaintiff No. 1 sold .4993 acre of land to others and the rest .1407 acres of land has been owning and possessing by the plaintiff. The defendant No. 1 claiming that he has acquired the suit land from the defendant No. 3 by way of Heva and soon he would enter the suit land. The plaintiff came to known on 16.07.1991. That the defendant No. 3 transferred .13 decimals of land to Nurjahan from the plot No. 138 vide registered deed No. 3061. Nurjahan had no title and interest over the suit land. So her husband the defendant No. 3 could not sell any land from the suit land. The defendant No. 3 has got some land after the death of his wife Nurjahan and he sold the land in favour of the plaintiff No. 1 and his brother Abdul Karim on 10.02.1965. The plaintiffs filed a suit before Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 63/1993 but the suit was filed with formal defect. So the plaintiffs withdrew the suit for filing fresh suit. The defendant No. 3, constructed a building in `Ga' schedule land which is owned by the plaintiff. So the plaintiff has filed this suit. 

 8. On perusal of the judgment passed by the learned trial Court, it appears, the learned trial Court on consideration of the evidence and materials on record found that the plaintiff Abdur Jabbar and his brother Abdul Karim were the owners of plot no. 138 and before that their mother Chandraban Bibi was the owners of plot no. 138 who vide heba-bil-eweaz deed dated 14.09.1949 exhibit-13 gifted the same in favour of heirs two sons Abdul Karim and Abdur Jabbar and in the said deed khatian number was written as 569 and plot number was written as 168, area of land was written 2.04; that in the right side of plot No. 168 in the said deed the word `illegible' was written; that in khatian No. 569 there was no dag as 168; that Chandraban Bibi was not the owner of plot No. 168 of khatian No. 190: that in exhibit-13 plot No. 168 has been wrongly written in place of correct number 138, but the boundary of plot No. 138 was given correctly; that the heirs of Abdul Karim having sold out their entire share in the said plot vide exhbit-4 and 4'ka' the defendants have no subsisting interest in the suit land that except defendant No.1 and 2, other defendants did not claim any interest in the suit land; that the defendant No. 1 and her husband defendant No. 3 got forceful possession in the suit land of schedule-Ga wherein the said defendants did not have any possession earlier. With these findings the learned trial Court decreed the suit. 

 12. Accordingly my assessment of evidence is as follows:- P.W.1 Abdur Jabbar in his deposition supported his case as made out in the plaint. He was cross-examined, but nothing contradictory came out in his cross-examination. P.W.2 Haji Din Mohammad Mollah though corroborated P.W. 1 but in cross-examination, stated that the plaintiff No.1 is his Mamato Bhai and the defendants are the heirs of another Mamato Bhai deceased Abdul Karim. He stated that in 1993 in the month of Ashyin/Kartic the defendant started constructing houses in the suit land and the plaintiffs resisted. In cross-examination only there was a suggestion that he is deposing falsely, but nothing material came out to disbelieve him. P.W.3 Abdul Azim stated in his examination in chief that the defendants dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land in October, 1993 and the plaintiffs resisted the defendants. However, in his cross-examination he admitted that he is the son in law of the plaintiff Abdur Jabbar. P.W.4 Md. Abdul Awal in examination in chief stated that both the plaintiffs and the predecessors of the defendants are his maternal uncle. He stated that Badsha Mia dispossessed the plaintiffs from some portion of the suit land in the month of Ashyin/Kartic in 1993. He was cross-examined thoroughly, however, in his cross-examination he admitted that he purchased some land from the plaintiffs and constructed house thereon. P.W.5 Ahmed Hossain is a witness who produced the volume of khatian No. 569.
